items.title: No event is confirmed single-entry by its structure sheet
items.detail: 15 of the 37 official Venetian structure sheets were read line-by-line in this pass (events #1, #2, #6-11, #13-15, #16, #18, #21, #22, #23, #25, #26, #28, #30, #54, #58, #59, #60, #61, #62, #63, #64 and the shared flight sheets). None of them states one-entry-per-player, no-re-entry, no-rebuy or no-add-on. The only sheet that speaks to multiple entries at all is the PokerAtlas Valuetown sheet, which prices 'all subsequent buy in's after the initial buy in' - that confirms extra entries ARE offered for events #18 and #58. Silence is not confirmation, so the qualifying list is empty until a sheet or the room itself says otherwise.
items.how_to_close: The monitor's first run audits all 37 sheets and quotes any rule sentence; anything still silent needs a written answer from the Venetian poker room (Q1).

items.title: 'TDA rules apply' was tested as a shortcut and rejected
items.detail: Every sheet says TDA rules apply, which raises the question whether the rulebook itself forbids re-entry by default. TDA's rule on re-buys (No. 29 in the 2026 set) governs procedure when re-buys are offered - players may not miss a hand, chips bought are in play behind, etc. It does not state that a tournament without an announcement is a freezeout. Using it as proof would be inference, so the unverified labels stay.
items.how_to_close: Ask the room to state the entry policy in writing (Q1), or find a sheet that says it.

items.title: No dated room rate for any property
items.detail: Official property pages advertise starting points and conditional poker rates; none publishes a dated total for a stay. Without check-in/check-out dates and an engine quote, the 'true cost per night' cannot be stated as a fact. The site publishes the fee/tax arithmetic and an editable rate field instead, clearly marked as an assumption.
items.how_to_close: Fix the dates and occupancy, then read the checkout total from the official booking engine for each candidate hotel and record it as a dated row in the rate log.

items.title: Room tax and cancellation terms were not re-read this session
items.detail: The 13.38% Clark County room tax figure, the $20/$40 parking figures and the cancellation language are carried from an earlier session's reading of the official hotel-terms page. This session tried four times on 2026-11-17 and the page did not load, so those numbers are labelled carried, not confirmed. The $55 resort fee WAS re-read today and is confirmed.
items.how_to_close: The monitor re-fetches the terms page and quotes the sentence; until then treat the tax input as unverified.

sources.label: Venetian hotel terms (not loading in this environment)

items.title: Cancellation deadline not captured for any property
items.detail: Cancellation policy is rate-specific and only appears with a dated quote. Nothing was captured, so the comparison is incomplete: a cheaper non-refundable rate is not like-for-like with a refundable one.
items.how_to_close: Read the deadline off each dated quote and store it in the rate log row.

items.title: No walking minute is verified for any hotel-venue pair
items.detail: No official page publishes door-to-door minutes, and this session refused to import third-party estimates as facts. Each pair carries a live map link so a number can be read and stored as a dated observation; until then the <=30 minute filter cannot pass anyone except by 'same property'.
items.how_to_close: Open each route link, read the walking time, and record it in walks.json with the date; the site then applies the filter for real.

items.title: No official finish time for any event
items.detail: Sheets publish start times and late-registration close, and for multi-flight events say a flight runs until about 12.5% of the field remain. Nothing states when play ends. Overlap flags are therefore stated as 'cannot both be registered for' or 'only possible if eliminated before X', never as a certainty.
items.how_to_close: Room confirmation of expected finish, or a published Day 1 scheduled end.

items.title: Four upcoming events publish no guarantee
items.detail: Events #3, #4, #5 (RaceDay Stack) and #6 have no guarantee line on their structure sheets and none in the calendar row, so guarantee/entry ratio is blank for them and they cannot be ranked on value. They are not assumed to be unguaranteed. Sheets #15 ($15,000 for events 29/31/34/38/42/50/51/53/55) and #16 ($75,000 for event #36) each state the guarantee as "(prize pool + total bounties)", so their guarantee is not comparable with a plain guarantee: those events stay in the separate bounty section and their GTD÷entry ratio is labelled bounty-inclusive. Sheets #18 and #29 print no guarantee line at all.
items.how_to_close: Ask the room whether a guarantee exists for those events.

items.title: 22 of 37 structure sheets are not audited in this pass yet
items.detail: The remaining sheets belong to satellites, bounty, seniors, ladies, tag-team, PLO and BIG O events. They sit in the separate section regardless of entry policy, and each row is labelled 'sheet not audited in this pass' rather than being treated as verified.
items.how_to_close: The monitor audits every sheet on its first run and this flag closes automatically if nothing new is confirmed.

sources.label: Structure-sheet URL pattern used by the monitor

items.title: The official Wynn poker URL serves the home page to non-browser fetchers
items.detail: Both https://wynnlasvegas.com/casino/poker (the form used by three earlier sessions) and https://www.wynnlasvegas.com/casino/poker returned the Wynn home page for this session on 2026-11-17, while search engines show poker content for the page. A scraper that only checks status codes would call that 'fine' and silently publish stale or wrong rows.
items.how_to_close: Fetch with a browser user-agent and compare the final URL and page title to the expected page; the monitor now records final_url + redirected so the dashboard shows it as a problem.

items.title: One schedule row sits on a page-chunk boundary
items.detail: The Nov 28 5:10 PM event #18 row's date cell was cut between chunks while reading the live calendar, so its date comes from the adjacent rows rather than from a directly-read cell. 93 of 94 rows were checked cell-by-cell (tools/check_rows.py reports 0 problems).
items.how_to_close: The monitor parses the whole table server-side each morning, which removes the chunking artefact.

items.title: COORDINATION.md carried unresolved merge markers on main
items.detail: Lines 133 and 150 contained '=======' and '>>>>>>> origin/main' plus a duplicated copy of the 60fb62da section - the file was committed with a half-resolved conflict. This session deleted only the marker lines and the duplicate copy (diff showed the retained section is a superset), and logged it on the board.
items.how_to_close: None - fixed in commit 4c396f3. Worth checking no other shared file carries markers.

items.title: Five parallel subsites plus the root dashboard all publish the same event data
items.detail: 60fb62da/, c07371e3/, df41f5c6/, strip/, verified/ and the root pages each hold their own snapshot with different labels for the same Venetian rows. Nothing reconciles them, so the same event can read 'verified' in one folder and 'unverified' in another. That is a decision hazard, not just untidiness.
items.how_to_close: Pick one canonical data source; publish others as read-only research archives with a banner. Suggestion S1 does this - awaiting your choice.

items.title: Earlier 'verified' claims are not uniformly verifiable
items.detail: Prior boards describe Wynn/Bellagio rows sourced from pages that now redirect or 404, and one folder marks rows 'verified' where the underlying sheet only stayed silent. This session publishes no row it could not re-read today.
items.how_to_close: Re-run the source check for every folder (the monitor covers the ones this site uses).

items.title: Occupancy and guest count are assumptions
items.detail: The rate log and the calculator assume 2 adults in 1 room because that is how the official date picker presents a quote. A single guest, a third guest, or a suite changes both the room rate and the fee coverage (the fee covers two people at the fitness facility).
items.how_to_close: State travellers and room count; the calculator takes it as an input.

items.title: No nightly budget or quality floor was supplied
items.detail: The brief makes cost and quality the higher priority, but no ceiling was given, so the site cannot rank hotels by value. It ranks only on confirmed fit (same property as the venue) and leaves quality blank.
items.how_to_close: Give a per-night ceiling and a minimum standard; then the shortlist becomes a real ranking.

items.title: No official quality metric is collected
items.detail: Star ratings and review scores come from third parties, which this project's rules exclude as evidence. With no official quality figure, 'quality is a higher priority than distance' cannot be applied; the site says so instead of guessing.
items.how_to_close: Choose the quality standard (official brand/tier, or an agreed third-party score with a dated observation).

items.title: Resort fee for Wynn / Bellagio / ARIA / Caesars properties not verified this session
items.detail: Only the Venetian/Palazzo fee ($55 + tax) was re-read today. Treasure Island's $49.95 and the 13.38% tax are carried from an earlier session. Other properties are blank rather than borrowed.
items.how_to_close: Re-read each property's official fee page; the monitor tracks those URLs.

items.title: Parking cost not re-read this session
items.detail: Carried from an earlier reading of the hotel terms page, which would not load for this session. Parking is only relevant if driving, and it is excluded from the nightly figures.
items.how_to_close: Re-read the terms page (monitor does it).

items.title: Monitor workflow needs a first real run on the default branch
items.detail: The daily re-check is wired as a scheduled GitHub Actions job that commits data back to the branch it ran on. Its first scheduled run after merge is what turns 'last checked' into a live value; the manual dispatch during this session is recorded below the table when it completes.
items.how_to_close: None - watch the Monitor page after the next run.

items.title: This repo already registers a workflow at `.github/workflows/site-check.yml`
items.detail: The Actions API lists an active workflow with that path named "Check Vegas Field Notes sub-site", owned by another session's branch; my gate was written to the same path and one of the two would have silently replaced the other. Mine is now `.github/workflows/poker4-site-verify.yml`. Nothing else in either file was changed — the other session's workflow is left as they published it, and the collision is reported here rather than resolved by me.
items.how_to_close: Owner decides whether both gates should exist; if not, delete one path.

items.title: Open PR #28 implements the same 14-item feature list on the root pages
items.detail: Session b6421d6a's PR #28 ("dashboard v2") adds a trip calculator, rate log, venue pages, monitor and verifier under root paths (index/hotels/schedule/calculator/tools/data-v2) while this branch ships the same features under poker4/. No file path overlaps in the diff itself, but both edit root index.html / README.md / COORDINATION.md, so whichever merges second will conflict. This is a duplicate-effort collision, not an error to auto-fix: both dashboards stay published and the merge order is left to the owner. Earlier merged PR #23 (98e4cb1c v2 monitor) also added .github/workflows/monitor.yml + v2-monitor.yml alongside this branch's tournament-monitor.yml.
items.how_to_close: Owner picks which dashboard is canonical; the other becomes an archive link.

items.title: Root `index.html` renders the "Other preserved research sets" section twice
items.detail: Present on `main` after the 2026-11-17 merges (one copy carries the v2/planner links, the other an older set). Both list the same subsites with different link sets, so a reader cannot tell which is current. Left exactly as `main` has it — this session only inserted its own link into the first copy — because silently editing another session's published section would hide the duplication.
items.how_to_close: Owner (or the root-page session) deletes one of the two sections.

items.title: Root `index.html` links `pages/index.html`, which does not exist in the repository
items.detail: Detected by the link check while resolving the merge of `origin/main` into this branch. `pages/` is not tracked, so the link 404s on GitHub Pages. Not created and not removed here: it belongs to another session's snapshot section, and inventing a page to satisfy it would be worse than the dead link.
items.how_to_close: The owning session either publishes pages/index.html or drops the link.
